title: Swap the Seats
story: Two parrots sit on the wrong perches. Without retyping their names, swap them.
goal: Swap the values: afterwards a must be "right" and b must be "left".
starter:
a = "left"
b = "right"
# swap them using only a and b (and maybe one helper variable)
hints: If you overwrite a first, the old value is gone. Where could you park it for a moment?
Use a third variable, temp: save one value in it, move the other, then use temp.

a = "left"
b = "right"
temp = a
a = b
b = temp
socratic: What happens to a if you write a = b first?
Where can the old value of a wait safely?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Swap the Seats”?
solution:
a = "left"
b = "right"
temp = a
a = b
b = temp
alt:
a = "left"
b = "right"
a, b = b, a

clean.label: Do the swap in one line (Python can assign two names at once)

tests.label: 3 lines in total, including the two starting lines
